Target audience: University students (CS/Engineering background)

Section: section_1 — The Core Problem: Contextual Ambiguity

Lecture lines:
Previous models processed words only linearly.
This misses dependencies across long distances.
Ambiguity arises when words shift meaning.

Planned animations:
Create text 'Word Ambiguity' in #FFFFFF color.
Display two similar words with changing highlights in #FFD700.
Add directional arrows #00FFFF between context and word.

Section: section_2 — The Intuition: Query, Key, and Value (QKV)

Lecture lines:
We treat retrieval like a search system.
Queries ask for what we need.
Keys label what is available.
Values contain the actual information content.

Planned animations:
Show Query vector #FF0000 targeting specific Key #00FF00.
Reveal Value vector #0000FF associated with that key.
Animate vector projection #FFFFFF for interaction visualization.

Section: section_3 — The Math: Visualizing Attention Weights

Lecture lines:
Attention matches queries to keys.
Higher scores indicate stronger relevance.
Softmax normalizes these scores to weights.

Planned animations:
Display matrix multiplication WQ * X in #FFFFFF.
Highlight dot product result in #FFD700 color.
Show Softmax normalization curve in #00FFFF color.

Section: section_4 — Self-Attention in Action

Lecture lines:
All words attend to each other simultaneously.
The model links related words directly.
This resolves long-range dependencies efficiently.

Planned animations:
Parallel heads visualized as stacked layers in #FF0000,#00FF00,#0000FF.
Synchronized movement to output space #FFFFFF.
Merge vectors into single final representation in #FFD700.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis: From Mechanism to LLMs

Lecture lines:
Stacking layers creates the Transformer.
Layers transform inputs into complex vectors.
These vectors capture deep semantic meaning.

Planned animations:
Display Transformer block icon in #FFFFFF color.
Show recursive sequence flow in #00FFFF color.
Zoom out to full model architecture in #FFD700.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: From Mechanism to LLMs", [
            "Stacking layers creates the Transformer.", 
            "Layers transform inputs into complex vectors.",

        ])

        transformer_icon.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(transformer_icon, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(transformer_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        flow = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF") for _ in range(5)])
        flow.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(flow, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(flow), run_time=1)
        self.play(flow.animate.shift(LEFT * 1.5), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        label = Text("Context Vector", font_size=20, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(label, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.play(transformer_icon.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)
